stories.narration: Côte d’Ivoire is already the world’s cocoa powerhouse. Now it wants a much bigger place in Africa’s gold economy. The government says the country’s first national gold-refining unit, in Abidjan, is expected to begin operations by the end of the first half of 2027. The refinery, developed through SIMEP, is designed to process up to one hundred tonnes of gold a year. But that number needs context. One hundred tonnes is refining capacity, not Côte d’Ivoire’s current mine output. The country produced 59.33 tonnes of gold in 2025, and officials projected about 62 tonnes for 2026. The ambition is much larger. By 2035, the government says it wants Côte d’Ivoire to become Africa’s largest gold producer. And this project is about more than one refinery. SIMEP is intended to connect semi-industrial mining, a national gold-buying desk, processing, international marketing and the creation of a state gold stock. The government says national investors will hold seventy percent of the company, with the state and SODEMI together holding forty-nine percent. StoneX is expected to support international marketing, while the buying system is also intended to improve traceability and bring more artisanal and small-scale gold into formal channels. That may be the bigger story. Côte d’Ivoire is not only trying to extract more gold. It is trying to control more of the value chain — from the mine, to the refinery, to the global market. For a country known worldwide for cocoa, gold could become the next major test of how much value can be processed and retained at home. This is Diajem Global Black News. Our People. Our Story. Our Own Way.
